countries.name: Singapore
countries.tagline: A city that runs on order, and somehow still surprises you.
countries.intro: My first stop into Southeast Asia — and the easiest place to fall for. Hawker centres, glass towers, and rainforest, all inside one MRT ride.

places.name: Marina Bay & the Downtown Core
places.note: Skyline walks, the Merlion at sunrise, and a rooftop that made me rethink what a city view could look like.

places.name: Tiong Bahru & Chinatown
places.note: Old shophouses, kopi in a real coffeeshop, and the best plate of chilli crab I've had anywhere.

places.name: Sentosa & Southern Islands
places.note: A short cable car ride out of the CBD chaos into beach clubs and quiet coastline.

logistics.stay: Capsule hotel, Bugis — clean, central, budget-friendly
logistics.transport: EZ-Link card on the MRT the entire trip — no car needed

countries.name: Malaysia
countries.tagline: Petronas lights, jungle air, and a food scene that never lets up.
countries.intro: KL was meant to be a two-day layover. It turned into a full week between the Batu Caves, the Cameron Highlands tea fields, and Penang's street art.

places.name: Kuala Lumpur
places.note: KLCC Park at golden hour, Batu Caves before the tour buses arrive, and Jalan Alor at night for the satay.

places.name: Cameron Highlands
places.getting_there: Drove up from Penang via Ipoh a few times, and also went straight by bus from Penang other times — both were a smooth, easy ride. Went back quite a few times while living in Malaysia.
places.note: Once up in the highlands, the easiest way in was just walking into one of the tourism centres in town and booking a day trip from there — Boh Tea Plantation was one of the best, with sweeping views over the rows of tea. Outside of that, there are hiking trails all through town and a little further out, worth wandering without much of a plan.

highlights.caption: Boh Tea Plantation
highlights.note: Endless rows of tea rolling over the hills — one of the best views from any of the day trips out of town.

places.name: Penang (George Town)
places.note: Street art alleys, colonial shophouses, and hands-down the best char kway teow of the whole trip.

logistics.stay: Mix of hostels (KL) and a homestay (Cameron Highlands)
logistics.transport: Rented a car for the highlands leg — Grab everywhere else
logistics.best_time: Year-round, avoid Nov–Dec monsoon on the east coast

countries.name: Thailand
countries.tagline: Temples at dawn, night markets at midnight, islands in between.
countries.intro: Three weeks, three regions — Bangkok's chaos, Chiang Mai's calm, and the islands down south. Still the trip I recommend to every first-time backpacker.

places.name: Bangkok
places.note: Wat Arun across the river at sunset, Chatuchak on a Saturday, and a rooftop bar that made the humidity worth it.

places.name: Chiang Mai & Pai
places.note: Rented a scooter and did the Pai loop over two days — waterfalls, canyon views, and the best banana pancakes on the route.

places.name: Koh Lipe & Koh Phi Phi
places.note: Island hopping by longtail boat, snorkeling off Maya Bay before the crowds arrived at 8am.

logistics.flights: Bangkok internal legs via Thai Lion Air + a ferry from Krabi to the islands
logistics.stay: Hostels in BKK & Chiang Mai, beach bungalow on Koh Lipe
logistics.transport: Scooter rental in the north, longtail boats in the south
logistics.best_time: Nov–Feb, dry season across the whole country

countries.name: Philippines
countries.tagline: Home base, and still the trip that surprises me every time.
countries.intro: 7,000+ islands and I've barely made a dent. These are the routes I keep coming back to — and sending friends on. Everything here is backpacker style — budget guesthouses over resorts, more time out on the water and in town than sitting in a hotel room.
countries.nav_tip: To keep navigation simple, I just searched the name of each place in Google Maps and followed the route — never had real difficulties doing it this way. That said, don't expect perfect roads everywhere; some destinations have a much rougher path than others.

places.name: Manila
places.getting_there: A 4-hour flight in from Malaysia to kick off the trip.
places.note: The sprawling starting point — colonial Intramuros, chaotic jeepneys, and a food scene that genuinely never sleeps.

places.name: Sagada
places.getting_there: About 6 hours by bus from Manila, through Baguio.
places.note: Mountain air, hanging coffins carved into limestone cliffs, and rice terraces that appear as the morning fog lifts.

places.name: Palawan
places.note: The Philippines' 'Last Frontier' — even the well-known corners still feel a little undiscovered.

sub_places.name: Coron
sub_places.note: Impossibly clear lagoons ringed by limestone karsts, with WWII shipwrecks resting in turquoise water just offshore.

places.name: Batangas
places.note: Two very different sides of the same province — a quiet freediving base and a long stretch of open beach, both easy trips from Manila.

sub_places.name: Mabini
sub_places.note: A quiet freediving base on the Verde Island Passage — one of the most biodiverse stretches of water on the planet.

sub_places.name: Calatagan
sub_places.note: Long stretches of pale sand and calm water — a low-key coastal escape without the crowds.

places.name: Bohol
places.note: Two visits, two very different sides — resort beaches in Panglao, and the quieter blue holes of Anda.

sub_places.name: Panglao
sub_places.getting_there: About a 1-hour flight from Manila to Tagbilaran.
sub_places.note: White sand beaches by day, and the otherworldly Chocolate Hills rolling across the interior.

sub_places.name: Anda
sub_places.getting_there: A 2-hour ferry from Siquijor into Tagbilaran, then a trike and bus out to Anda — mostly used as a stop on the way to Camiguin this time. We also rented a motorbike and drove up to Chocolate Hills — about a 2-hour ride from Jagna Port.
sub_places.note: Bohol's quieter side — untouched beaches and blue holes, without Panglao's resort crowds.

highlights.caption: Chocolate Hills
highlights.note: Thousands of grass-covered mounds that turn cocoa-brown in the dry season, seen here from the lookout point above them.

places.name: Bicol
places.getting_there: A 2-day motorbike ride from Manila, with overnight stops in Pagbilao and Naga City.
places.note: Mayon Volcano's near-perfect cone watches over the road the whole way, with some of the country's spiciest food waiting at the end of it.

places.name: Romblon
places.note: The 'Marble Capital of the Philippines' — quiet fishing towns, marble quarries, and coastline that barely sees a tourist.

places.name: Sibuyan
places.note: Known as the 'Galapagos of Asia' — dense rainforest, rivers running gin-clear, and Mt. Guiting-Guiting looming over all of it.

places.name: Siquijor
places.getting_there: Flight from Manila to Dumaguete (1 hour), a quick trike to the port, then a short ferry over to the island. We rented a motorbike right at the port for all 5 days on the island — there are plenty of rental stalls there and you don't need to book ahead. I pre-booked with 'Bibings Car & Motorbike Rentals' (found them on Facebook) since I wanted a specific type of bike — their shop is right next to the port too, and they gave a good discount for renting more than 2 days.
places.note: An island wrapped in old mysticism, with waterfalls the colour of glass tucked into the jungle.

highlights.caption: Cambugahay Falls
highlights.note: A multi-level waterfall you can swim and jump between — go early, since it gets crowded with tour groups after around noon.

places.name: Camiguin
places.getting_there: A 4-hour ferry from Jagna, Bohol. Getting back out: ferry to Balingoan, bus to Cagayan de Oro, overnight, then a flight home to Manila. We rented a motorbike from where we stayed, Marianita's Cottages, for all 4 days on the island.
places.note: More volcanoes than towns, with two very different landmarks worth the trip.

highlights.caption: White Island
highlights.note: A pure white sandbar sitting in open water off the coast, with Camiguin's volcanoes as a backdrop — no shade, no structures, just sand and sea for as far as the tide allows.

highlights.caption: Sunken Cemetery
highlights.note: A cemetery swallowed by the sea after a volcanic eruption in 1871, marked today by a large cross rising out of the water just offshore — you can swim, snorkel, or take a short boat out to it.

places.name: Hoi An & Da Nang

places.name: Ho Chi Minh City
places.note: War Remnants Museum, the Bến Thành night market, and rooftop pho that broke every rule I thought pho had.

countries.tagline: The one where the ocean did all the talking.
countries.intro: Proof you don't need an overwater villa budget to see it properly — local islands, a guesthouse, and some of the clearest water I've ever swum in.

places.name: Maafushi (Local Island)

countries.name: India
countries.tagline: A country too big for one trip — this was chapter one.

places.name: Delhi

countries.name: South Korea
countries.tagline: One island, one week, and somehow still not enough time.
countries.intro: A week on Jeju with three friends — rented a car, split the stay between the island's north and south, and packed in more quirky attractions than I can fully list.
countries.nav_tip: If halal food matters to you, you'll find far more options closer to Jeju City than the more remote parts of the island.

places.name: Jeju
places.getting_there: Flew in as a group of four (Malaysian, Filipino, and Indian passports) — Jeju was visa-free for all of us at the time. Rented a car for the week; a Malaysian driving licence was enough to drive locally, no international permit needed.
places.note: Cool, rainy weather the whole trip, and somehow still one of the most scenic weeks of the entire run — waterfalls, cliffs, tea fields, freediving grandmothers, and a genuinely wild range of quirky museums packed onto one island (the Museum of Sex and Health included). The standout was Udo Island — a ferry out from Seongsanpo Port, then a full day cycling the coastline, capped off with the famous peanut ice cream before the evening ferry back. Right at the same port, we also climbed Seongsan Ilchulbong to the top — the views over the crater and coastline from up there were incredible. Saeyeongyo Bridge was another good stop for the views alone. We also caught local haenyeo (women freedivers) fishing just offshore, which was something else to watch in person.

sub_places.note: Base for the first half of the week, including the day trip out to Udo Island.

sub_places.note: Base for the second half — right near Jeongbang Waterfall and the southern coastline.
